counterexample: Let V={s,t,u,v}, S={s,u}, T={v,t}, S'={s,v}, and T'={u,t}. Then S∩T'={u} and T∩S'={v}. Thus the edge u→v goes precisely from S∩T' to T∩S', so it is included in c(S∩T',T∩S'), contrary to step 0024. For a full instance satisfying the preceding minimum-cut assumptions when zero capacities are allowed, take edges s→t of capacity 1 and u→v of capacity 0. Every (s,t)-cut has capacity 1, so both displayed cuts are minimum, while u→v is still an edge from {u} to {v} in the allegedly absent term.
assessment_summary: Steps 0001–0023 can be read consistently, with the expression in step 0020 interpreted as the total capacity of edges between the indicated subsets. Step 0024 is definitively false: its own stated memberships place u→v inside, not outside, c(S∩T',T∩S'). The subsequent counting argument therefore is not justified.
